To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synaptic transmission and passive membrane properties of hippocampal CA1 pyramidals are not altered during the first 48 h after a period of global brain ischemia.
synaptic transmission and passive electrical properties of CA1 neurons are preserved in the early phase of the post-ischemia period, but are severely altered in the later phase.
the synaptic transmission in the post-ischaemic hippocampus was preserved until the time of the neuronal degeneration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of ischemia on the electrophysiological properties of the hippocampus.
the electrophysiological properties of neurons in the rat hippocampus following a period of transient cerebral ischemia.
the mechanisms of neuronal death in the hippocampus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although there is a significant reduction in the size of the population spike 2 days following ischemia, the basic properties of the hippocampal CA1 neurons are not altered.

in CA1 pyramidale neurons of the septal pole of the hippocampal formation, synaptic transmission is preserved in the early postischemic period and neuronal properties are unaltered up until 48 h after an episode of ischemia.
there are no significant differences between the electrophysiological characteristics of neurons in the post-is-chemic period and those in control animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ischemia-induced neuronal death is preceded by a selective loss of excitatory synapses.
the ischemic insult does not induce any changes in synaptic transmission or neuronal excitability in the hippocampus that would predispose the CA1 pyramidals to death.

the hippocampal slices are an excellent model to study the mechanisms underlying ischemic neuronal damage and that the hippocampus is a good candidate to investigate mechanisms underlying ischemic damage in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, at least in the hippocampal CA1 region, the first 24 h after a 20 min period of global cerebral ischemia are characterized by a relative functional stability of the neurons and their synapses.
the CA1 pyramical cells are very resistant to ischemic insult.
the CA1 pyramides in the septal hippocampal slices are not altered in the first 48 hours after ischemia.
